'''Benedetto Vigna''' (born 10 April 1969) is an Italian [[physicist]] who is the [[chief executive officer]] of the automotive company [[Ferrari]].

==Career==
Born in [[Potenza]], [[Basilicata]], he grew up in the neighboring municipality of [[Pietrapertosa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ondanews.it/il-lucano-benedetto-vigna-dal-1-settembre-amministratore-delegato-ferrari-orgoglio-e-senso-di-responsabilita/|title=Il lucano Benedetto Vigna dal 1° settembre amministratore delegato Ferrari. "Orgoglio e senso di responsabilità"|language=IT|date=8 August 2021|access-date=19 December 2021}}</ref>

Graduating with honors as a [[physicist]] from the [[University of Pisa]] in 1993, he did his first experiences at the [[CERN]] in [[Geneva]], the [[European Synchrotron Radiation Facility|ESFR]] in [[Grenoble]], and the [[Max Planck Institute]] in [[Munich]]. In 1995 he started working for [[STMicroelectronics]] starting the company's commitment to [[microelectromechanical systems]] (MEMS).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.st.com/content/ccc/resource/corporate/company/company_presentation/77/73/ad/6f/06/be/42/57/vigna_it.pdf/files/vigna_it.pdf/jcr:content/translations/en.vigna_it.pdf|title=Biografia di Benedetto Vigna|language=Italian|work=[[STMicroelectronics]]|access-date=13 November 2021}}</ref> He worked for a year at The Berkeley Sensor & Actuator Center (BSAC) at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], before returning to ST and appointed director of the MEMS Business Unit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eetimes.com/analog-profile-benedetto-vigna/|title=Analog Profile: Benedetto Vigna|website=eetimes.com|date=19 August 2008|access-date=7 October 2025}}</ref>

Vigna's team developed the [[Three-Axis Acceleration Switch|three-axis accelerometer]], a three-dimensional motion [[sensor]] which was initially applied to the [[airbags]] of automobiles.<ref name=nintendo>{{cite news|title=Premio per l'inventore europeo. In gara anche un italiano|url=https://www.corriere.it/cronache/10_marzo_12/premio-inventore-europeo_3c3a8e6e-2e05-11df-ab2a-00144f02aabe.shtml|first=Giovanni|last=de Paola|language=Italian|magazine=[[Corriere della Sera]]|date=12 March 2010|access-date=13 November 2021}}</ref> After reducing its size and cost, the sensor was used in the [[Nintendo Wii]] console's wireless controller and [[iPhone]]'s screen rotation feature.<ref name=nintendo/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eetimes.com/theres-more-to-mems-than-meets-the-iphone/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CThe%20accelerometer%20can%20recognize%20any,a%20speakerphone%20on%20the%20back.|title=There’s more to MEMS than meets the iPhone|website=eetimes.com|date=9 July 2007|access-date=7 October 2025}}</ref> For this invention, Vigna was included in the shortlist of twelve candidates for the "European Inventor 2010" award promoted by [[European Patent Organization]].<ref name=nintendo/> In his career he has registered more than two hundred patents.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://worldwide.espacenet.com/searchResults?DB=EPODOC&IN=vigna&PA=ST%20MICROELECTRONICS&ST=advanced&compact=false&locale=en_EP|title=Benedetto Vigna Result list|work=[[Espacenet]]|access-date=13 November 2021}}</ref> In 2015, he received the [[IEEE Frederik Philips Award]] "for leadership in conceiving, developing,
and commercializing micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS)".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://corporate-awards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/philips-rl.pdf|title="IEEE Frederik Philips Award" recipients|website=corporate-awards.ieee.org|access-date=7 October 2025}}</ref>

On 9 June 2021, he was announced as the new [[chief executive officer]] of [[Ferrari]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ferrari.com/en-GB/articles/ferrari-appoints-benedetto-vigna-as-chief-executive-officer|title=Ferrari appoints Benedetto Vigna as chief executive officer|work=[[Ferrari]]|date=9 June 2021|access-date=13 November 2021}}</ref>
